author: w495
scope: special case: maximum of m independent standard Gaussians
reproduction: With Q(t)=1/m, s=t+1/t, Mills gives Q(s)/Q(t)>=a=(2/5)e^(-3/2), t^2<=2log m. Independent-copy variance is at least (1/4)(1-e^(-a))/t^2>=c/log m. For the upper bound, OU covariance plus hypercontractivity gives integral_0^1 m^(-(1-u)/(1+u))du<=2/log m; the factor m comes from summing the m indicator derivatives.
remaining_gap: This is an extremal-value lemma, not a power bound for C0120.

author: w495
reproduction: Each prefix U_i is N(0,r); no independence among prefixes is used. For R=max_i|U_i|, P(R^2>x)<=min(1,2m e^(-x/(2r))). Splitting the tail integral at 2r log(2m) yields E R^2<=2r(log(2m)+1), and |M-A|<=R pointwise.
remaining_gap: Graph grows with r and has exponential layer width; it is not the source lattice.

author: w495
scope: exact first-chaos mass for special graph
reproduction: Gaussian integration by parts makes first-chaos coefficient P(v on maximizing path). Tree symmetry gives 2^(-k) at each of 2^k internal vertices at level k, and 1/m on each of mn private-chain vertices. Sum of squares is (2-2/m)+n/m=3-2/m, since n=m. The unique maximizing path has L indicator derivatives, so Dirichlet energy is L.
remaining_gap: Small first-chaos mass does not control higher chaos mass on the source lattice.

author: w495
scope: variance order on the special graph
reproduction: Centered L2 triangle gives |sqrt Var M-sqrt Var A|<=sqrt B. Under B<=c n/(4log m), L1 yields Var M>=c n/(4log m) and Var M<6n/log m. B=O(r^2), while n/log m=2^r/(r log2), so the condition holds eventually. L=n+r is comparable with n.
remaining_gap: No contradiction to C0120 on the fixed east/north lattice.

author: w495
scope: fixed-beta positive-temperature extension on the special graph
reproduction: Soft-max gives M-log m/beta<=F_beta<=M, hence E(F_beta-A)^2<=2B+2(log m/beta)^2=o(n/log m) for fixed beta. The centered L2 bounds of L4 apply. Gibbs path masses sum to one; symmetry makes expected mass of each chain 1/m and internal vertex 2^(-k), preserving first-chaos variance 3-2/m.
remaining_gap: This is a different finite-temperature model on a changing graph; beta must stay fixed.

author: w496
reproduction: For the finite Gaussian path maximum, the a.e. gradient is the n-site indicator path; Hermite Dirichlet identity gives sum_k k v_nk=n. For k>K, sum v_nk<=n/(K+1), giving the displayed conditional criterion. OU gradient covariance has coefficients k v_nk e^(-(k-1)u), and integrating e^(-u) recovers sum v_nk.
remaining_gap: No polynomial bound on the actual lattice low-chaos mass is supplied.

author: w496
reproduction: Each path visits one vertex in each V_t. A_t has variance 1/(t+1), and Cov(A_t,g_v-A_t)=0 on its layer. Joint Gaussianity and layer independence make A independent of all residuals, so M_n=sum A_t+M_n(R) and Var M_n=H_n+Var M_n(R).
remaining_gap: The residuals are correlated within layers; the iid theorem cannot be reapplied to them.

author: w496
reproduction: For normalized H_k, Var(sqrt(n/k)H_k(G))=n/k and E|D(sqrt(n/k)H_k(G))|^2=n. With k=ceil(log n), fixed-degree mass vanishes and fixed-u gradient correlation is e^(-(k-1)u), but n/k has no fixed power saving.
remaining_gap: The function is neither a convex path maximum nor globally Lipschitz.

author: w496
scope: Gaussian fan graph outside fixed lattice
reproduction: M_fan=g_root+sqrt(n-1)W_n. Mills and separated quantile events give Var(W_n)>=r0/(8log n). For noise rho=e^(-u), union bound on coincident maximizing branches gives P(I=I_u)<=2e^(-nQ(a))+n^(1-2alpha/(1+rho)). Setting u=16loglog n/log n and alpha=(3+rho)/4 makes the terms vanish as exp[-(log n)^(7/2+o(1))] and (log n)^(-4+o(1)).
remaining_gap: Fan root degree grows with n, so this does not refute C0120 on Z^2.
